title: Variational Quantum Factorization (VQF) using Different Variations of Quantum Approximate Optimization Algorithm (QAOA)
journal_or_venue: 2025 17th International Conference on Communication Systems and Networks (COMSNETS) - Workshop on Quantum Technologies (WQT)
abstract_summary: This paper implements Variational Quantum Factoring (VQF) on the Qiskit simulator and compares four QAOA variants (standard QAOA, multi-angle QAOA, CVaR QAOA, and CVaR multi-angle QAOA) for factoring small bi- and tri-prime numbers on NISQ-style hardware. Experiments factoring 143, 291311, and 175 (using 4, 6, and 3 qubits respectively) show that multi-angle QAOA and its CVaR-enhanced variant generally yield the highest success probabilities (e.g., 0.92 for 143 and 0.99 for 175).
methodology_description: The authors implement Variational Quantum Factoring (VQF) by mapping integer factorization into a binary optimization problem, simplifying multiplication-derived Boolean clauses, forming a squared-clause objective function, reducing interaction order (to at most 3-body terms), and mapping classical bits to qubit operators via ak -> (I - σz_k)/2 to obtain an Ising-type problem Hamiltonian H_c. They implement QAOA-style variational circuits on the Qiskit simulation framework: building an ansatz of p alternating layers of e^{-i γ H_c} and e^{-i β H_M} (with H_M = -Σσ_x) and decomposing the Hamiltonian unitaries into native gates (Rz, Rzz, Rzzz, Rx). They compare four algorithmic variations: standard QAOA, multi-angle QAOA (maQAOA, where each gate has its own angle), CVaR QAOA (expectation computed over the top N_α measurement outcomes), and CVar maQAOA. A classical optimizer is used in a feedback loop to minimize the chosen objective (expectation value or CVaR objective) over the variational parameters. After optimization the circuits are sampled and measurement outcomes are post-processed to extract candidate factors (from bitstrings) and compute a success probability (fraction of samples whose decoded factors multiply to the target number). Experiments factor three integers (143, 291311, 175), exploring different circuit depths p and CVaR α fractions, and report success probabilities for each algorithmic variant.
algorithms_used: Conditional Value at Risk QAOA (CVaR QAOA)
experimental_setup: All experiments were carried out on the Qiskit quantum simulation framework. Problem Hamiltonians (Ising form) were decomposed into native multi-qubit rotations (Rz, Rzz, Rzzz) and single-qubit Rx rotations for the mixer. Variational circuits with p alternating layers were executed in simulation; a classical optimizer minimized either the mean energy or the CVaR objective. Measurement sampling was used to compute success probabilities. No physical QPU or specific noise model is reported.

results_summary: This conference paper reports Qiskit-simulated implementations of Variational Quantum Factoring (VQF) using several QAOA variants. The authors apply standard QAOA, multi-angle QAOA (maQAOA), CVaR QAOA, and CVaR maQAOA to three integers (143, 291311, 175) using 4, 6, and 3 qubits respectively. Their simulations indicate that maQAOA and CVaR-maQAOA (with certain α choices) typically produce the highest success probabilities. They report peak success probabilities of 0.92 (143), 0.56 (291311), and 0.99 (175). The paper also notes that success does not scale uniformly with circuit depth across instances and attributes poorer results on larger instances to increased Hamiltonian/circuit complexity.
performance_claims: [supported] 143 factored (simulation) using 4 qubits with peak success probability 0.92 achieved by maQAOA (or CVaR-maQAOA with α=1).
[supported] 291311 factored (simulation) using 6 qubits with peak success probability 0.56 achieved by CVaR-maQAOA with α=0.75.
[supported] 175 factored (simulation) using 3 qubits with peak success probability 0.99 achieved by maQAOA (or CVaR-maQAOA with α=1).
[supported] The multi-angle QAOA (maQAOA) ansatz increases the number of variational parameters compared to standard QAOA and empirically improved success probability in these simulated instances.
[supported] The CVaR objective (using top-fraction α of measurement outcomes) can improve optimization performance for some instances; example α=0.75 helped for 291311.
quantum_advantage_detail: The paper suggests VQF (with advanced QAOA variants) is a promising NISQ-era approach for factoring larger numbers than current Shor demonstrations, but provides only Qiskit simulation results and does not demonstrate a provable or empirical quantum computational advantage over classical factoring methods or full implementations on hardware. Thus claims of practical quantum advantage remain speculative.
